acceptance_evidence: Author replied inline (comment 3195725761): 'checked in the database this litterally never happens so yeah on the one hand that would make it valuable if it ever does, but on the other hand probably not worth it' — no code change; the `contact.user?.id` optional-chain + `if (userId !== undefined ...)` pattern is unchanged in the final pre-merge commit (18963cc0, line 901-902), no logger.warn added.
description: In the Pass-1 actor contact-role lookup, `contact.user?.id` optional-chains past a hypothetically-null `user` on a row already filtered by `user_id IN (actorUserIds)`, so if MikroORM ever returned a partial row with null user, the entry would silently drop into Pass 2 with no log line marking the contract violation. Reviewer proposed an explicit undefined guard plus a warn log instead of silent degradation.

acceptance_evidence: Author replied 'Applied' (comment 3195741073); commit e06d784 rewrites the onConflictMergeFields comment to state the frozen-snapshot principle for all seven frozen fields (sender/actor refs, roles, party types, entity link) instead of naming only two.
description: The `actorUser` FK reference is frozen on re-ingest as a side effect of being absent from `onConflictMergeFields`, but the adjacent code comment only named `senderContactRole`/`actorContactRole` as frozen, leaving the FK-freeze behavior undocumented and its intentionality ambiguous for a future reader.

acceptance_evidence: Author replied 'Already addressed in the latest push — D-12 is now inside deriveContactRole(email, user, permissionsRoles)...' (comment 3195752999); commit e06d784 ('centralise D-12 OPS_FALLBACK in deriveContactRole') moves the fallback out of upsertContacts and into the shared helper used by both sender and actor paths, with a new integration test pinning the convergence.
description: The D-12 `OPS_FALLBACK_EMAILS` chain was applied post-hoc in the sender path (`upsertContacts`) but not inside `deriveContactRole` used by the actor's Step-2 derivation, so a future user-less ops mailbox would resolve to `'ops'` as a sender but `null` as an actor — an unobserved-in-prod but real path divergence.

acceptance_evidence: Dedicated commit 18963cc0 ('remove dead afterEach + vi imports from adapter integration test') removes both afterEach(vi.restoreAllMocks()) blocks and the afterEach/vi imports, exactly matching the recommendation.
description: Two `afterEach(() => { vi.restoreAllMocks(); })` blocks in this integration test file are dead code since the file contains zero `vi.spyOn`/`vi.fn`/`vi.mock` calls, likely copy-pasted from the co-located spec file; reviewer noted 86% of sibling case-radar integration tests carry no such afterEach.

acceptance_evidence: Author replied 'Applied' (comment 3195819870); commit 9b0d8a0 adds 'Adapter integration: frozen-snapshot on re-ingest (mutate live contact role, re-ingest same sourceRecordId, assert role unchanged)'.
description: No runtime integration test verified `actorContactRole` frozen-snapshot semantics on re-ingest — the existing unit test only asserted the shape of `onConflictMergeFields`, not that a re-ingest actually leaves the persisted role untouched, so a wrong conflict target or MikroORM-generated SQL bug would go undetected.

acceptance_evidence: Author replied 'Applied' (comment 3195828658); commit 9b0d8a0 adds 'Adapter integration: soft-deleted actor user → null role at runtime (catches bypass of User softDelete @Filter)'.
description: The runtime path for a soft-deleted actor user (post-loop null-fill in `resolveActorContactRoleByUserId`) had no adapter-level integration test, even though the analogous SQL backfill path was covered — a regression in the User entity's softDelete filter or a switch to `disableFilters: true` would silently populate a deleted user's role with no test catching it.

acceptance_evidence: Author replied 'Applied' (comment 3195846139); commit 9b0d8a0 adds 'Adapter integration: mixed Pass-1 / Pass-2 actors in same batch (exercises Set/filter boundary in resolveActorContactRoleByUserId)'.
description: No test combined a Pass-1 actor (contact row hit) and a Pass-2 actor (contact row absent) within the same ingest batch, leaving the Set/filter logic in `resolveActorContactRoleByUserId` unverified for realistic multi-actor batches and its Pass-1/Pass-2 boundary handling untested.

acceptance_evidence: Author replied 'Applied' (comment 3195888954); commit 9b0d8a0 adds 'SQL backfill: actor with CommunicationContact.contactRole=null falls through Step 1 to Step 2 (different code path from the TS resolver)'.
description: No SQL backfill test covered an actor whose `CommunicationContact` row exists but has `contact_role IS NULL`, a case Step 1 silently skips (via the `cc.contact_role IS NOT NULL` predicate) leaving Step 2 to derive the role through an independent JOIN path the TS resolver's tests can't stand in for.

acceptance_evidence: Author reply (comment 3195952849) describes adding the counterpart test ('selects user.role when its rank beats permissions_grant... together they catch a <= -> >= inversion'); commit 9b0d8a0 adds 'SQL backfill: user.role beats permissions_grant when its rank is lower (counterpart to the existing lawyer-vs-lead test)'.
description: The `<=` tie-break operator in the equal-rank comparison between `best_permissions_role` and `filtered_user_role` documents that permissions_grant wins ties, but no test exercised equal-rank inputs, so a future accidental change from `<=` to `<` would silently flip tie-break behavior with nothing to catch it.

acceptance_evidence: Commit 9b0d8a0 adds 'SQL backfill: multiple permissions_grant rows resolve to the most specific regardless of insertion order (two actors with reversed insertion orders, both resolve to lawyer)', directly matching the recommended test.
description: The `LIMIT 1 ORDER BY array_position(...)` subquery picking the most-specific permissions_grant for a multi-grant user had no test seeding multiple grants, leaving the ordering/determinism of this core Step-2 logic — which touches ~40k production rows in a one-shot migration — unverified.

acceptance_evidence: Commit 9b0d8a0 adds 'SQL backfill: unranked user.role + unranked permissions_grant + no contact row -> actor_contact_role stays null AND step2 = 0 rows updated (proves the WHERE-clause guard is doing its job)', directly matching the recommended test.
description: No test covered an active actor whose `user.role` is unranked and who has no ranked `permissions_grant`, a case the WHERE clause excludes so the role stays NULL; without a test, a future loosening of the `ANY(role_ranks)` filter or the OR-clause exclusion could silently start attaching a wrong role to these rows.

acceptance_evidence: Commit 9b0d8a0 diff shows the exact annotation added: 'Unreachable: outer WHERE (best_permissions_role IS NOT NULL OR filtered_user_role IS NOT NULL) excludes both-null rows from the UPDATE. Kept as an explicit guard so a future WHERE-clause loosening does not silently write NULL through the idempotency check on re-runs.'
description: The `ELSE NULL` branch in the role-selection CASE expression is unreachable because the outer WHERE clause already excludes rows where both candidate roles are NULL; left unannotated, it's a maintenance trap where a future loosening of the WHERE clause would cause this branch to start silently writing NULL through the idempotency guard.

acceptance_evidence: Commit 9b0d8a0 message: 'backfill-actor-contact-role.integration.test.ts: move client.connect() inside the try block; swallow client.end() errors so cleanup noise can't mask the original throw' — matches the recommendation verbatim.
description: `await client.connect()` sat outside the surrounding try block in the backfill integration test helper, so if connect() threw, the finally block's `client.end()` cleanup would never run, risking deferred error events / unhandled-rejection noise leaking into later tests.

acceptance_evidence: Commit 9b0d8a0 adds 'DTO: trim accept-path for actorContactRole (\'  paralegal  \' -> \'paralegal\')', matching the recommended test exactly.
description: The DTO schema's `.trim()` accept-path for `actorContactRole` was untested — only the reject path (all-whitespace collapsing to null) was covered — so a value like `'  paralegal  '` trimming correctly to `'paralegal'` had no regression guard; removing `.trim()` accidentally would ship whitespace-padded values undetected.

acceptance_evidence: Commit 9b0d8a0 adds 'DTO: non-string degrades to null via .catch(null) (numeric input)', matching the recommended test exactly.
description: The `.catch(null)` soft-parse behavior for `actorContactRole` on type-mismatched (non-string) input had no test, so removing that catch clause would turn a backward-compatibility safety net into a hard validation failure with nothing to flag the regression.

acceptance_evidence: Commit 9b0d8a0 adds 'Service spec: pin actorContactRole pass-through in findContext (mirrors the existing findByUser pin; same serializeMessage but different code path)', matching the recommendation exactly.
description: The `findByUser` test pinned `actorContactRole` pass-through through `serializeMessage`, but the parallel `findContext` test exercising the same private method did not assert on the field, so a future change dropping the field in the `findContext` code path specifically would go uncaught.

acceptance_evidence: Commit 9b0d8a0 message: 'communication.utils.spec.ts: replace process.cwd-based path arithmetic with `?raw` imports via the @/ alias — CWD-independent, no path counting, no runtime fs.'
description: A test resolved a SQL fixture path via `resolve(process.cwd(), '..', '..', relativePath)`, assuming the Vitest runner's CWD is `apps/api` with no enforcement; a CWD shift (monorepo-root invocation, IDE runner, config change) would surface as an opaque ENOENT instead of a meaningful drift-detection failure.

acceptance_evidence: Commit 9b0d8a0 message: 'case-radar.seeder.ts: rewrite misleading comment about lawyer contactRole (round-robin per STAFF_CONTACT_ROLES_FOR_QA, not always co-counsel); the real Step-2-skip invariant is contact row always exists for lawyerUsers, not role is co-counsel.'
description: A code comment claimed lawyerUsers' seeded contacts always have `contactRole='co-counsel'`, but the actual upstream seeding rotates through `STAFF_CONTACT_ROLES_FOR_QA` by index (lawyer/paralegal/co-counsel round-robin); the runtime code itself was correct, only the comment misstated the real invariant (contact row always exists, not that the role is fixed).
